newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-AUSTRALIANS WIN MEN'S U.S. OPEN DOUBLES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRALIANS WIN MEN'S U.S. OPEN DOUBLES.

text.p: Top-seeded Australians Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde finished the Grand Slam season on a high note on Friday with a rare U.S. Open repeat victory in the men's doubles.

The Australians, popularly known as the Woodies, beat eighth-seeded Dutchmen Paul Haarhuis and Jacco Eltingh 4-6 7-6 7-6 to become the first duo to successfully defend the U.S. Open doubles title in the Open era.
The last to accomplish the feat were another Australian pair, Roy Emerson and Fred Stolle, in 1965 and 1966.
The Woodies crowned another successful season that saw them win their fourth successive Wimbledon championship and take Olympic gold in Atlanta.

In Friday's final they dominated each of the tiebreakers, surging from 3-4 to win the second-set tiebreak 7-5 and racing out to a 4-0 lead on the way to winning the climactic decider 7-2 and clinching the $240,000 first prize.
Winners of 38 career titles, the Woodies will undoubtedly go down in history as one of the best doubles teams.
"I guess it is a combination of points, of strengths and weaknesses that we have, and we communicate very well on the court," Woodforde said when asked about their success.
"We are able to cover each other's weaknesses."
"It was a very satisfying win," Woodbridge said. "They beat us in the final here two years ago."
Haarhuis said of the Australians: "They have all the shots you need for doubles."
Friday's victory gave Woodbridge-Woodforde a 6-4 edge over the Dutch duo.
